questions.prompt: Directions: For this part , you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay titled“Are people becoming addicted to technology?”.The statement given below is for your reference. You should write at least 120 words but no more than 180 words. Numerous studies claim that addiction to technology is real and it has the same effect on the brain as drug addiction.
questions.correctAnswer:
Are People Becoming Addicted to Technology?

Technology has become part of almost every activity, and some people find it difficult to put their devices away. Although frequent use alone does not prove addiction, losing control over that use deserves attention.

For example, a student may plan to check one message before studying, only to spend an hour watching short videos. If this pattern repeatedly harms sleep, schoolwork or relationships, it is more than a harmless habit. However, technology also enables useful learning and communication, so blaming every device would be unreasonable. The important issue is whether a person can choose when to stop.

We should therefore develop practical boundaries. Turning off unnecessary notifications, setting aside time without screens and seeking support when daily life is seriously affected can help. Technology ought to serve our goals. Recognizing unhealthy patterns early allows us to enjoy its advantages without letting it control our attention.

questions.explanation:
以下为按题意独立写成的参考范文，作文没有唯一答案。标题回应是否上瘾；先界定问题再谈边界，不把所有科技使用都称为成瘾，也不把题面研究说成确凿医学结论。

题目要求讨论成瘾，开头先写使用科技本身正常，再界定难以控制、影响学习生活的过量使用；主体举不断查看手机的情境；结尾给使用边界。addicted to后接名词，set limits是设置限制，concentration是注意力。题面研究是引导讨论的材料，范文不需要当作已经核验的医学证明。判断词可用some、may、can保留范围；自查是否回答标题问题并具体说明什么行为才值得关注。

练习方法：先用提示列三段提纲，在30分钟内独立写作，再按下方标准逐项打分；把失分最多的一段重写。参考范文约151词（缩写、连字符词按一词，含标题或书信称呼落款），满足120–180词要求；评分用于练习自检，不代表官方阅卷分数。
rubric: 练习自评总分15分：题目覆盖0–6＋结构0–4＋语言0–5，先独立写完再对照；观点不同于范文也可得满分，只要有合理支持。
题目覆盖0–6分：该题检查——区分经常用设备与失控使用，用影响学习生活的例子支持观点。。6分=任务完整且有具体理由/活动/例证；4–5分=切题但细节偏薄；2–3分=遗漏主要任务；0–1分=基本离题。
结构0–4分：4分=开头明确任务、主体按逻辑展开、结尾回扣，段间自然；3分=顺序清楚但局部衔接生硬；1–2分=跳跃或机械罗列；0分=内容难以组织理解。
语言0–5分：5分=语法和用词基本准确、句型有变化；3–4分=少量错误但不影响理解；1–2分=反复出现时态、主谓一致或搭配错误并影响阅读；0分=多数句子不能理解。
格式与修订：按原题保持120–180词；新闻/书信/提案用对应体裁，明确要求的首句逐字保留。若超限、少写任务或缺必要格式，先修改再评分，不把字数达标当作内容满分。

questions.prompt: The number of people experiencing depression shows a sharp increase in the first year of high school.
questions.passage:
The start of high school doesn't have to be stressful

A) This month, more than 4 million students across the nation will begin high school. Many will do well. But many will not. Consider that nearly two-thirds of students will experience the "ninth-grade shock," which refers to a dramatic drop in a student's academic performance. Some students cope with this shock by avoiding challenges. For instance, they may drop difficult coursework. Others may experience a hopelessness that results in failing their core classes, such as English, science and math.

B) This should matter a great deal to parents, teachers and policymakers. Ultimately it should matter to the students themselves and society at large, because students' experience of transitioning(过渡) to the ninth grade can have long-term consequences not only for the students themselves but for their home communities. We make these observations as research psychologists who have studied how schools and families can help young people thrive.

C) In the new global economy, students who fail to finish the ninth grade with passing grades in college preparatory coursework are very unlikely to graduate on time and go on to get jobs. One study has calculated that the lifetime benefit to the local economy for a single additional student who completes high school is half a million dollars or more. This is based on higher earnings and avoided costs in health care, crime, welfare dependence and other things.

D) The consequences of doing poorly in the ninth grade can impact more than students' ability to find a good job. It can also impact the extent to which they enjoy life. Students lose many of the friends they turned to for support when they move from the eighth to the ninth grade. One study of ninth-grade students found that 50 percent of friendships among ninth graders changed from one month to the next, signaling striking instability in friendships.

E) In addition, studies find the first year of high school typically shows one of the greatest increases in depression of any year over the lifespan. Researchers think that one explanation is that ties to friends are broken while academic demands are rising. Furthermore, most adult cases of clinical depression first emerge in adolescence(青春期). 逐句核对：地点层级Xiping Town, Anxi County, Fujian Province不可错位；throughout Anxi说明全县，不是全福建。in all four seasons与spring and autumn分别表达全年采摘及两季最优。Processing…作主语，requires specialized skills and extensive experience保留技术、经验双条件。vitamins用复数，distinctive taste译独特口感。末句三项依次prevent heart disease、lower blood pressure、improve memory；按题面保留，但不扩大为保证治愈疾病。
rubric: 练习自评总分15分：信息准确0–8＋语法0–5＋表达0–2；允许拆句、换同义词，不要求逐字匹配参考译文。
信息准确0–8分：逐项检查——铁观音地位；福建安溪西坪及全县差异；四季采摘春秋最佳；技术经验；维生素口感；心脏、血压、记忆。8分=全部关键信息正确；6–7分=少量次要细节遗漏；3–5分=多处遗漏/数字或关系误译；0–2分=核心人物、动作或逻辑严重错误。
语法0–5分：5分=时态、单复数、主谓一致、从句和介词基本正确；3–4分=少量错误仍易理解；1–2分=多处错误妨碍理解；0分=主要句子结构不可理解。
表达0–2分：2分=用词搭配自然、因果转折时间衔接清楚；1分=可理解但有中文式生硬表达；0分=词序/词义造成大面积理解困难。
修订操作：先在中文原题划出时间、数量、地点和连接词，再在自己的译文逐项找对应；为每处漏译或误译写一句修正。此分数是练习估计，不是官方阅卷或机器评分。
